newsitem.title: UK: Unstable times ahead for aluminium industry - Bird.
newsitem.headline: Unstable times ahead for aluminium industry - Bird.

text.p: The aluminium market is heading for an unstable time during the remainder of the decade as supply growth fails to match that of consumption, industry analysts Anthony Bird Associates said in their latest report.
The report said prices have "over-reacted to the industry's short term oversupply."
"As a result they are threatening to exacerbate the medium to long term supply shortages which will threaten before long," it added.
The report forecast aluminium to average at $1,572 a tonne in 1996, $1,723 in 1997, $2,351 in 1998 and $2,828 in 1999.

The Western world market is forecast to be in surplus by 479,000 tonnes this year, but a small deficit of 81,000 tonnes is expected next year before widening to 665,000 tonnes in 1998 and 730,000 tonnes in 1999.
Bird said production costs continued to fall in recent months partly because of weaker alumina prices.
He estimated average operating costs on a total world basis at $1,253 a tonne. Western smelters averaged $1,202 while in the CIS costs were much higher at $1,427.
"At such operating costs, today's prices are uncomfortable, but not impossible," Bird said.
"Far more serious is the fact that current prices fall well short of the full costs in a new smelter, inclusive of capital servicing. That would mean a price of $1,591," he added.
